Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT P1 - spike in 502s for POST /v1/generate in us-west-2. Error rate jumped from ~0.5% to 18% at ~2026-03-15T02:00Z. Paging #oncall.
Alejandro M: I'm on it, joining the call. grabbing logs from the runtime.
Sam R: I'm available to take a 30m handoff if needed. Any obvious alerts?
Oncall Bot: Alerts: high-5xx-rate (/v1/generate) in us-west-2; autoscaler firing scale-ups; increased queue depth on worker-pool-gpu-a. Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-01.
Nisha P: Pasting top error from the request log: 
```
[2026-03-15T01:58:42Z] request_id=abc123 host=worker-12 err=502 upstream=runtime timeout kv-cache:put timeout=2000ms
[2026-03-15T01:59:01Z] request_id=def456 host=worker-7 err=502 upstream=runtime reason=load-shed queue_depth=128
```
Alejandro M: Interesting — some hosts show kv-cache timeouts, others show load-shed. Kayla, can you confirm control plane shows any rollout changes?
Kayla B: Console shows a canary rollout for model-opt-v2 at 2026-03-15T00:50Z targeted to us-west-2 (10%). Control plane audit shows config_version=125.
Alejandro M: Runtime agent on worker-12 shows config_version=124. That smells like propagation lag.
Prod SRE: Data point: netstat and iowait on worker-7 is normal. CPU is fine, GPU utilization at ~70%. The queue depth spike looks correlated with requests being routed to a variant that can't serve (different kernel combo).
Sam R: If control plane thinks 10% are canary but half the agents haven't picked up config 125, routing mismatch could be steering traffic to incompatible model variants -> 502s. Hypothesis A: control-plane->data-plane config propagation failed for some agents. Hypothesis B: the canary model has a regression causing internal timeouts on certain sequence lengths.
Nisha P: I pulled a sample of failing request payloads — many have long context (~12k tokens). The canary model-opt-v2 has an entry that triggers a slower kernel path when seq>8k. Could explain higher latency and kv-cache timeouts.
Alejandro M: Mitigation proposal: 1) Pause rollout (control plane) to stop further assignments to canary. 2) Route existing in-flight traffic to fallback model-opt-v1 by forcing routing policy. 3) Increase short-term capacity for GPU pool to drain queues. Who can flip the rollout?
Kayla B: I can pause the rollout now from console: doing it.
OpsBot: rollout pause succeeded (config 126 staged).
Alejandro M: Now force-route: running the emergency routing toggle: 
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/emergency-route" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"route_override":"model-opt-v1","region":"us-west-2"}'
```
Nisha P: Output: {"status":"ok","applied_agents":15,"pending_agents":3} -> three agents still pending.
Sam R: For the pending agents, I'm SSH'ing to worker-7 to restart runtime agent to pick up config 126.
Sam R: restart command: `sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime` -> restart completed.
Sam R: After restart, worker-7 logs show config_version=126 and health=ok. Observed immediate drop in 502s for that host.
Nisha P: System metrics: global 5xx rate dropped from 18% to 4% in ~90s after rollout pause + route override. Queue depth decreasing.
Kayla B: Console/API discrepancy noted: Console showed rollout as paused immediately; control-plane audit shows config 126 dispatched, but the API-based agent list (agents API) still returned old entries for 3 agents until they restarted. Need to capture why those three didn't stream config updates.
Prod SRE: Capturing candidate root causes: (1) control-plane streaming connection TLS reneg for agents 7/12, (2) agent crash loop prevented apply, (3) partial banker upgrade mismatch causing kernel incompatibility.
Alejandro M: Tasks: A) Collect agent logs from pending agents (Sam). B) Capture control plane broadcast logs and delivery receipts (Kayla). C) Run synthetic long-context requests on canary vs prod to reproduce (Nisha). D) Customer impact list (Prod SRE).
Sam R: Copied logs for worker-7/12 -> attaching important snippets: 
```
worker-12: ERROR controller: failed to apply config 125 -> checksum mismatch -> applied 124
worker-7: WARN connect: stream reset by peer, reconnecting
```
Sam R: For worker-12 checksum mismatch seems like agenst cached old artifact. I'm pulling /var/lib/redwood/model-manifest to inspect.
Nisha P: Repro script I ran: 
```
for i in {1..5}; do curl -s -X POST $ENDPOINT -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @long_ctx.json; sleep 0.5; done
```
Nisha P: On model-opt-v2 container, one request hit a kernel path that took 3.4s per token for a section, causing kv-cache eviction. On v1 it was 0.4s. That supports the regression hypothesis.
Kayla B: I'm pulling control-plane broker logs: I see transient connection errors to agent stream for worker-12 at 2026-03-15T01:57:40Z. Delivery retry policy ran but the agent didn't ack because it had older manifest checksum.
Prod SRE: Customer impact: affected keys scoped to hosted customers in us-west-2 with larger context workloads; estimated 12 active customers, 3 had noticeable failures and retried. Logged ticket IDs: CUST-4981, CUST-4987, CUST-4992. We should notify support and account teams.
Alejandro M: For immediate mitigation we've paused rollout and forced routing. Next steps during mitigation: collect full timeline and create in-incident RCA doc. Sam, upload the agent logs to the incident folder. Kayla, export control-plane audit & delivery receipts (include broker IDs). Nisha, attach the repro artifacts and perf traces. Prod SRE, prepare customer impact summary and comms draft.
Sam R: Uploaded logs to s3://incidents/INC-2026-03-15-01/agents/*.gz and linked in thread: https://internal/share/INC-2026-03-15-01/logs
Kayla B: Exported control plane traces and attached delivery receipts. Broker trace: broker-3 had a transient CPU spike around 01:57Z causing backpressure.
Nisha P: Repro artifacts uploaded: long_ctx.json, perf traces, and a short jupyter with kernel flame graphs. Link: https://internal/share/INC-2026-03-15-01/repro
Prod SRE: Customer impact doc: https://internal/share/INC-2026-03-15-01/customer_impact.md — includes affected API keys and observed error windows.
Alejandro M: Hypothesis tracking in-thread: 
- H1 (control-plane propagation lag): evidence = mismatched config_version (124 vs 126), agent logs (stream reset); mitigation (pause + force-route) improved errors -> supported.
- H2 (model regression on v2 for long-context): evidence = repro shows kernel slowdown -> supported.
- H3 (data-plane resource exhaustion): evidence weaker, GPU/cpu utilis OK for most hosts -> less likely.
Kayla B: Consensus: incident is multi-factor: control-plane delivery issues exposed a canary regression that only manifested at scale for long-context requests. Root cause will likely be combination of control-plane broker backpressure + canary regression.
Prod SRE: Minutes for on-call handoff: Sam will own post-mitigation monitoring for next 2 hours, Alejandro will draft RCA outline, Kayla and Nisha will collaborate on root cause evidence. OpsBot: creating follow-up task list and assigning owners.
OpsBot: tasks created: T-1243 (collect agent manifests) assigned Sam R; T-1244 (broker capacity investigation) assigned Kayla B; T-1245 (model regression debug) assigned Nisha P; T-1246 (customer comms) assigned Prod SRE.
Sam R: I'll keep this thread updated with any bounce backs. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
Alejandro M: Adding final note: we'll run a controlled canary rollback to v1 for any remaining gradual rollouts until we have a patch for v2's kernel path. RCA doc draft will include timeline (attach logs + timestamps) and a proposed action: improve delivery acking, stronger manifest checksum handling, and add pre-rollout long-context perf checks.
Kayla B: Noted. Closing the active paging loop. If any new 5xx spikes reappear, ping @oncall immediately.
Oncall Bot: Incident status: mitigated. All immediate mitigations applied.
Prod SRE: last check at 02:22Z shows 5xx rate back to baseline. Marking incident as mitigated in tracker.
